items.q: Hi Mr Ashby, I'm Priya, one of the third-year medical students.
items.note: greeting/name in the same turn is fine (extra conversation matches don't count)

items.q: What's brought you along to clinic today?
So when did you first start noticing you were getting breathless?
Did the breathlessness come on all of a sudden or has it crept up on you gradually?
items.note: follow-up onset-gradual (scored as its parent fact)

items.q: How much can you do these days before you get SOB?
how many blocks can u walk before you have to stop and catch your breath?
And can you get up a flight of stairs without having to stop?
Do you ever feel out of breath when you're just sat resting?
items.note: follow-up exertion-rest; British 'sat'; about breathing at rest, not the chest-pain-at-rest negative

items.q: Have you had any CP or tightness in your chest?
What does the chest discomfort actually feel like - sharp, dull, squeezing?
Whereabouts is the tightness and does it go anywhere else like your arm or jaw or back
items.note: follow-up chest-location; run-on, no question mark

items.q: Does the chest tightness ease off once you stop and rest?
items.note: follow-up chest-relief; mentions rest but asks what relieves exertional tightness, not the chest-pain-at-rest negative

items.q: On a scale of 0 to 10 how bad does the chest pain get at its worst?
Do you ever get chest pain when you're resting, not doing anything at all?
items.note: pertinent negative; contrast with the chest-relief follow-up

items.q: You mentioned you nearly fainted, can you tell me a bit more about that?
Have you had any dizzy spells or felt like you might keel over?
What were you doing at the time you nearly fainted?
Did you get any warning beforehand, like your vision going grey or feeling sweaty?
items.note: follow-up presyncope-warning; 'vision' should not pull to focal neuro

items.q: Do you go lightheaded when you stand up quickly out of a chair?
Did you actually black out completely?
Was there any shaking or jerking, or did you bite your tongue?
That must've been really scary, nearly passing out like that.
items.note: mentions the near-faint but is an empathy statement, not a question

items.q: Any palpitations, or feeling your heart racing or fluttering?
Do you get breathless lying flat or wake up at night gasping for air?
items.note: orthopnoea and PND in one turn; both are the same negative

items.q: Have you noticed your ankles getting puffy?
Any tenderness in your calves or one leg swollen up?
items.note: DVT screen; one-sided, not the bilateral ankle swelling negative

items.q: Any cough or temperatures recently?
Any weakness in your arms or legs, or slurred speech?
Has your weight changed at all over the last few months?
Have you been feeling more tired or run down than usual?
Have you been getting any headaches lately?
items.note: case target list has nothing on headaches

items.q: Any change in your bowel habit, like constipation or diarrhoea?
items.note: British spelling of diarrhea; not covered by the case

items.q: Do you get any pain or burning when you pass urine?
items.note: dysuria; not covered by the case

items.q: Has a doctor ever told you that you have a heart murmur?
Have you ever been told there's a problem with any of your heart valves?
When you were young did you ever have rheumatic fever?
items.note: 'fever' should not pull to the fever/chills negative

items.q: Could you tell me whether you have any long-term medical conditions?
How long have you had the high blood presure for?
Have you ever had any surgery or been admitted to hospital?
Are you on any regular medicaton at the moment?
Do you ever forget to take your tablets?
any allergys to medicines that you know of?
Has anyone in your family had heart trouble or died suddenly?
And have you ever been a smoker?
How many cigarettes a day did you smoke, and when did you give up?
items.note: follow-ups smoking-amount + smoking-quit, both scored as the smoking fact

items.q: Do you drink alcohol, and have you ever taken any street drugs?
Are you still working or are you retired now?
Who's at home with you?
Do you do any regular exercise, like swimming or going to the gym?
items.note: general exercise habit, not the exertional limit

items.q: What's most important to you in your life at the moment?
What sort of things do you normally eat in a day?
Are you currently in a sexual relationship?
So do you have any thoughts yourself on what might be causing all this?
What were you hoping we'd be able to do for you today?
items.note: expectations (ICE); target covers concerns and expectations

items.q: Who's your favourite football team?
Did you manage to find parking alright this morning?
Do you know if the café downstairs is open yet?
Thanks so much for talking to me today, that's been really helpful.
Would you mind if I had a listen to your heart now?
Could you lean forward for me and breathe all the way out, then hold it?
items.note: positioning instruction for auscultation; breathing words should not pull to the breathlessness facts
